introduction-testing-is-not-enough.core: Tests check the interleavings you thought of; distributed bugs hide in rare orderings of messages, crashes and retries that tests almost never hit. Formal methods let you specify a design precisely and exhaustively check all behaviours (within bounds) against invariants, finding design flaws before code exists. AWS, Azure and MongoDB use TLA+ to catch such bugs.

first_principles.problem: A replication protocol passes thousands of tests, then loses data in production under a rare crash-and-retry sequence.
truths: The state space of concurrent systems is enormous.
Rare interleavings still happen at scale.
Designs can be wrong before code is written.
derivation: **Model check** all interleavings in small configurations.

analogy.title: Checking every possible chess move sequence for a rule flaw
analogy.story: Playing a few games won't reveal it; exhaustive analysis will.
analogy.breaks: Chess is finite but huge; model checkers bound the system size to stay tractable.

flow: Model checker found a 35-step bug trace

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A bug tests would likely never reach.

check.q: Why do tests often miss distributed-system bugs?
check.a: Bugs depend on rare orderings of messages and failures that tests rarely produce.

what-is-tla.core: TLA+ (Temporal Logic of Actions, Leslie Lamport) describes systems as state machines: variables, an initial-state predicate (Init), a next-state relation (Next) of possible actions, and properties: invariants that must hold in every state, and temporal properties (eventually, always) about behaviours. It's mathematics (sets, functions, logic), not code.

first_principles.problem: Design documents describe protocols in prose that hides ambiguity.

analogy.title: A board game's rulebook written in precise maths
analogy.story: Every legal move is defined, so you can prove certain positions are impossible.
analogy.breaks: Board games have one rulebook; TLA+ specs abstract away implementation detail you must later map to code.

steps.label: Check
steps.detail: TLC proves Inv holds in every reachable state.

code.text:
VARIABLES x
Init == x = 0
Incr == x < 3 /\ x' = x + 1
Reset == x = 3 /\ x' = 0
Next == Incr \/ Reset
Inv == x \in 0..3

check.q: What does the Next formula define in a TLA+ spec?
check.a: All possible state transitions (actions) the system can take.

pluscal-a-gentle-bridge-to-the-math.core: PlusCal is an algorithm language that looks like pseudocode (processes, variables, while loops, labels marking atomic steps, either/or for nondeterminism) and translates into TLA+. It's an easier on-ramp for engineers, letting them model concurrent and distributed algorithms and check them with TLC.

first_principles.problem: Engineers find raw TLA+ notation intimidating and never start writing specs.

analogy.title: Writing a story outline before the formal script
analogy.story: It's easier to start with the outline, then convert it into the precise script.
analogy.breaks: Outlines lose detail; PlusCal translates mechanically into equivalent TLA+.

steps.label: Finding
steps.detail: Both read 0, both write 1: lost update found.

check.q: What do labels mean in PlusCal?
check.a: They delimit atomic steps; everything between two labels executes as one transition.

the-model-checker-tlc-the-ultimate-bug-h.core: TLC explores every reachable state of a spec for a finite configuration (e.g. 3 nodes, 2 values, bounded message counts), checking invariants and temporal properties. On a violation it prints a minimal error trace, the exact sequence of steps reaching the bad state. Symmetry sets and state constraints keep exploration tractable.

first_principles.problem: A design review can't convince anyone the protocol never loses acknowledged writes.
truths: Small configurations reveal most bugs (small-scope hypothesis).

analogy.title: A maze solver that tries every corridor
analogy.story: If there's any path to the dragon, it will find it and draw the route.
analogy.breaks: Mazes are finite; real systems aren't, so TLC checks bounded models.

example.title: Config file

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Millions of states checked in minutes.

code.text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}  Values = {v1, v2}
INVARIANT NoTwoLeadersInSameTerm
INVARIANT CommittedNeverLost
CONSTRAINT MaxTerm

example.outcome: rare bugs found with concrete traces.

check.a: Most design bugs can be found by checking small configurations exhaustively.

what-tla-finds-in-practice.core: In practice TLA+ finds lost updates from unsafe interleavings, split-brain from stale leaders, liveness bugs like deadlocks or endless retries, incorrect recovery after crashes, membership-change errors and subtle assumptions about message ordering. Teams report gaining design clarity and confidence to make aggressive optimisations safely.

first_principles.problem: A team wants to justify the time cost of writing specs.
truths: Design bugs are expensive in production.

analogy.title: A wind tunnel for designs
analogy.story: You find aerodynamic flaws on the model, not after the plane is built.
analogy.breaks: Wind tunnel models are scaled physically; specs abstract logic, so implementation bugs can still occur.

example.title: Cache invalidation protocol
flow: Spec of cache + DB + invalidation messages
TLC finds: delayed invalidation after newer write → stale cache forever

check.q: What does TLA+ not guarantee about your implementation?
check.a: That the code matches the spec; implementation bugs can still exist.
